channel.title: The Talas Herald
channel.description: News from Talas and across Irad.

item.title: TSU dates Bronze Age site near Kara-Suu rock art to 1500–1200 BCE, tentatively
item.description: About 40 red-ochre horses and riders were recorded in a rock shelter beside a settlement; the site is fenced, but the 1997 heritage ordinance does not reach it.

item.title: 146 MW Chatkal hydro cascade planned; no cost, financing or contractor published
item.description: The plan equals about a tenth of Toktogul's 1,440 MW, and its upper stations would need the consent of the Naiman and Sarybagysh clans.

item.title: Farm output hits IS 6.1bn in nine months; volume up 12%, value only 6%
item.description: The Ministry of Economy's preliminary estimate shows the record harvest lifting tonnage faster than income, with potato prices falling in the glut.

item.title: Maksat says valley farmland should stop becoming house plots; no rule changed
item.description: The Lieutenant Governor asked the Ministry of Economy to count converted arable land, while district-level approvals continue as before.

item.title: French edition of Turkestan memoir out; Iradi memoirs still lack a translator
item.description: A French edition of "The Sorrow of Turkestan" appeared this month, while Chernov's 2001 and Orozbekov's 2012 memoirs remain unavailable in any foreign language.

item.title: Kazakh-Chinese driverless truck trials leave Irad's hauliers outside the planning
item.description: No announced route crosses the ISEZ, and Iradi plates are not recognised in Kazakhstan, so freight at Chu Gate and Talas North Terminal still runs on Kyrgyz paper and human drivers.

item.title: Snow leopard station opens at Uuk-Bulak; releases on tribal land need clan consent
item.description: The TSU-run Ilbirs Station has five enclosures and a field laboratory, but no written agreement with the Chatkal clans and no fund for herders' losses.

item.title: Maksat floats 9,000 bpd refinery at Kochkor-Ata; no investor, crude or cost named
item.description: The plant would be about a fifth the size of Nurzhan's, serving southern districts where diesel costs up to 3.65 som a litre more than at NurGaz pumps.

item.title: Caspian container backlog reaches Irad only through Kazakh routes, traders say
item.description: Irad has no port, no ship and no say in Middle Corridor capacity, but every box bound for Talas or Nurzhan crosses a neighbour first.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan caps coal for 90 days; Irad's buyers rely on merchants' own prices
item.description: Households in Jogorku and the southern districts are filling sheds from Tash-Kömür yards, as Nurzhan's air index hit 161 on Friday.

item.title: Before banning potato imports, publish the storage survey
item.description: A record crop is good news for growers, but the draft order to 1 March rests on stocks nobody outside the ministry has been shown.

item.title: Irad files 268-glacier inventory with COP17 through Bishkek; it has no seat
item.description: The ministry and TSU paper argues that glacier data belong in the 2027 Naryn schedule, but nobody has said whether the secretariat will log it.

item.title: Kyrgyz-Belarus 30-day registration waiver would reach only Iradis holding Kyrgyz passports
item.description: Minsk is a minor route next to Russia and Kazakhstan, and the ISEZ has no consulate there and no arrangement with Belarus.

item.title: Samarkand talks on US trade proceed without Irad, though all three claimants attend
item.description: The ISEZ has no seat or observer status in the C5+1 format, while the US keeps Talas Air Base 12 km from the city.

item.title: Power exports reach 99% of annual plan, 2.92bn kWh, with ten weeks still to run
item.description: Iradenergo says winter supply to Talas and Nurzhan is covered, but the dollar income and the clans' share remain unpublished.

item.title: Attelkom's China fibre link opens at 400 Gbps; price of the capacity not disclosed
item.description: The route south along State Route 1 hands over to a Kyrgyz carrier at Suzak, with no state-level agreement behind it and the Department of Public Information's block lists still in force.

item.title: Bank of Irad puts nine-month growth at 9.4%, behind Kyrgyzstan's 10.8%
item.description: The estimate is preliminary and counted in som at the 8.40 peg, while the bazaar rate runs 11 to 12.

item.title: Nurzhan Compute Park: $450m, 40 MW rising to 150 MW, but partners unnamed
item.description: The Lieutenant Governor toured the gas-fired data-centre site on Monday and promised 300 jobs; gas volumes, cooling water and who pays for the grid link were not given.

item.title: Kervan Elektrik to run Nurzhan, Chu and Kara-Buura grids; loss target is 11%
item.description: The Turkish operator, already running Talas, takes over metering and billing under a 15-year contract, while the utility keeps the wires and Toktogul revenue stays outside the deal.

item.title: Heat plant gas conversions would put IS 670 million on Talas and Nurzhan bills
item.description: University sensors logged 71 days above an alert level in Nurzhan's Dastgoh last winter, yet private-house stoves are outside the plan.

item.title: Kyrgyz FDI of $1.3bn is 4.5 times Irad's inflow, Bank of Irad figures show
item.description: Most of the ISEZ's US$286 million in 2025 went to energy and minerals, and over half was reinvested profit from firms already here.

item.title: Draft ban on potato imports to 1 March tests whether the record crop will keep
item.description: Imports were under 7% of last year's supply, ministry figures show, but they arrived in the late-winter weeks when stored local stocks run short.

item.title: EU grants Kyrgyzstan €6m for school reforms, paid on results
item.description: The budget support, about 592 million Kyrgyz som, goes to the treasury in Bishkek; the ISEZ has no EU channel of its own, though many Iradi families use Kyrgyz schools.

item.title: Name the partners before public money goes into Sary-Bulak
item.description: The antimony restart is welcome news for the district, but two sets of official figures disagree and IS 114 million rests on backers nobody will name.

item.title: First business census runs to 30 November; bazaar stalls and farms are the test
item.description: Officials put the unobserved economy at 23% of output and 60% of farm turnover, and firms must answer or face fines.

item.title: Kyrgyz fish plant opens near Bishkek with 3,000-tonne capacity
item.description: Talas traders say the Alamudun plant matters less for its size than for who owns the cold chain between Chui region and the Kichi-Korgon crossing.

item.title: Kyrgyz fuel output up 1.9-fold; Irad's diesel still rests on one refinery
item.description: Bishkek's statistics show a near doubling in nine months, but no public record shows any of it reaching ISEZ pumps, where bus fares rise on Monday.

item.title: Kyrgyz building output up 1.6-fold; Talas permits rose 13%, costs 18%
item.description: Bishkek's statisticians report a construction surge, while Talas planning records show a smaller rise in approvals and a steeper one in the price of finishing a flat.

item.title: Record harvest of 210,000 tonnes of potatoes leaves growers paid less than bazaar prices suggest
item.description: Grain output is up about 40 per cent on 2025 at 1.2 million tonnes, but storage, not supply, will decide who gains from the glut, growers and an economist say.

item.title: Bishkek revives metro plan despite its own planners' cost and demand finding
item.description: Talas economists say the dispute is a lesson in who pays for rail transit in a city of about a million people, and no Iradi budget could carry one.
